# RustyNES v2.8.0 — "Bulkhead"

The first release of the v2.8.x line that [ADR 0041](https://github.com/doublegate/RustyNES/blob/main/docs/adr/0041-hardware-release-is-v3.0.0.md) put before the SuperStation One core (**v3.0.0**). It acts on the libretro audit's findings about the boundary between the RustyNES core and RetroArch: what happens there when something goes wrong, what the core hands the frontend, and what it gets back. Every finding in it was shown failing by a test that drives the core exactly as a frontend does, before it was fixed.

**For RetroArch users:** an internal error no longer closes RetroArch, save states keep working after you select the Zapper, a closed game no longer leaves RetroArch holding pointers into freed memory, and the core loads from frontends that do not support libretro's newer game-info command. **Emulation behaviour does not change**: AccuracyCoin 144/144, nestest, and every golden are as before. **The MiSTer sibling does not change, and no new bitstream is cut.** No hardware has run any bitstream; the board session is v2.9.2.

## An internal error stops the game, not RetroArch

A panic anywhere inside a frame, such as a mapper invariant or an unexpected missing value, crossed the C boundary between the core and RetroArch and aborted RetroArch outright, with no chance to write a battery save. Seven unchecked assumptions sat on the frame path alone.

Fixing this took two changes, and the first is the one that is easy to miss. The shipped core was built to **abort** on a panic (the workspace release profile says so), which means no panic handler inside it could ever run: a test would pass, because tests unwind, while the core RetroArch loads still aborted. The libretro core is now built to **unwind** on every supported path (the crate `Makefile`, the libretro buildbot, and the pull-request cross-compile gate). Cargo cannot set this per crate, so a direct `cargo build --release` still produces an aborting core: it now warns when built that way, and says so in RetroArch's log when a game loads. The desktop and web builds keep aborting.

Then every core callback that runs emulation stops a panic at its own boundary. The game stops, and every later call is refused until the game is unloaded. The console is deliberately **kept**, not freed: RetroArch holds raw pointers into its memory, and freeing it, which is what the audit proposed, would have turned a crash into a use-after-free. Kept, the battery save is still there for RetroArch to write. Reloading the game carries on. Removing the new handler reproduces the old failure exactly: the test process dies with "non-unwinding panic", as RetroArch did.

The core's messages, that one included, now go to RetroArch's own log through libretro's log interface. They used to go to stderr, which RetroArch does not put in its log.

Unwinding is not free, so it was measured before being adopted. The frame path gains the unwind tables and landing pads the compiler now keeps: **about 0.1% more retired instructions per frame** (`perf stat`, +0.097% and +0.108% on the two frame workloads), a difference the timing benchmarks cannot resolve from noise, and a 4.4% larger core. The desktop build is unaffected. Details: [`docs/performance.md`](https://github.com/doublegate/RustyNES/blob/main/docs/performance.md).

## Save states that survive a Zapper

RetroArch asks a core once, at load, how large its save states are, and sizes every save-state, rewind and run-ahead buffer from that one answer. RustyNES measured its state at load, when both controller ports read "unplugged". Selecting the Zapper plugs it in on the next frame, the state grows, and every save after that failed. The core now reserves room for the largest expansion device on both ports (26 bytes) and zeroes what it does not use; the save-state reader treats an all-zero tail as padding. A test that encodes every supported device pins the reserve to the largest one exactly.

## Closing a game clears RetroArch's memory maps

The core hands RetroArch pointers into its RAM, battery RAM and nametable RAM, which its cheat search and RetroAchievements read directly. RetroArch keeps those until the whole core is unloaded, not when a game closes, so after closing a game it held pointers into freed memory. The core now replaces them with an empty map before freeing the console; RetroArch's handler discards the old ones first.

## Loading from any libretro frontend

The core only loaded through `GET_GAME_INFO_EXT`, an optional libretro command, and refused every frontend that does not answer it. The reason was one layer down: the Rust binding the core uses (`rust-libretro-sys` 0.3.2) generates libretro's standard `retro_game_info` as an empty one-byte struct, so the game a frontend passes never reached the core. The binding is unmaintained, so it is now **vendored** with that struct written out by hand (`vendor/rust-libretro-sys`, MIT, credited in `NOTICE`; the two-line patch is documented in its `VENDORED.md`), and the core falls back to the standard path: the game's bytes, or the file at its path. Restoring the original binding no longer compiles, which is the proof the patch is the one in use. A frontend that answers that command with only a path now takes the same route instead of getting an error.

## The save state is complete

- **The 2A03's internal data bus is saved.** It is a separate latch from the open bus a DMC fetch drives, and it was missing from the save state. Leaving it stale never changed a frame over 1,500 restores on three ROMs (the next opcode fetch overwrites it first), so this completes the state rather than fixing an observed desync. States from earlier releases still load.
- **The save-state schema audit now covers the bus**, not only the CPU, PPU and APU. Added, it reported 49 bus fields; one was the real gap above, and the other 48 are now classified with written reasons.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| AccuracyCoin (RAM decoder) | 144 / 144 |
| nestest | pass |
| `--features test-roms` workspace suite | 154 suites, 2,735 passed, 0 failed |
| libretro C-ABI harness | 16 passed |
| Mutations | each fix reverted in turn turns its test red: containment, poisoning, drop-on-panic, map withdrawal, save-state headroom, zeroed tail, the device maximum, the load fallback; the unpatched binding fails to compile |
| fmt, clippy `-D warnings` (every CI feature set, both wasm32), rustdoc `-D warnings`, `no_std`, `cargo deny` licences | clean |

**Not run here:** the libretro buildbot's Apple, Android and webOS jobs, which build the vendored binding and the unwinding core on images this machine does not have. The pull-request gate rehearses the Linux, Windows and Arm triples.

**Next: v2.8.1**, the libretro build and metadata fixes (Makefile targets, the symbol version script, input and audio polish, and the `.info` extensions), then the RTL releases v2.8.2 to v2.8.4.

## Install

- Download the pre-built binaries for Linux, macOS, and Windows below.
- The WebAssembly build is live at [doublegate.github.io/RustyNES](https://doublegate.github.io/RustyNES/).
- The RetroArch core is in RetroArch's Online Updater on the platforms the libretro buildbot publishes to.
- The audit ledger is [`docs/audits/libretro-disposition.md`](https://github.com/doublegate/RustyNES/blob/main/docs/audits/libretro-disposition.md), and the plan [`to-dos/plans/v2.8.0-bulkhead-plan.md`](https://github.com/doublegate/RustyNES/blob/main/to-dos/plans/v2.8.0-bulkhead-plan.md).
